note: T-3333. The lights people made in the town of 1 July 1835, drawn when Settings › Time of day darkens it (renderers/web/js/night-lights.js). Every window pane in the town and the fort can glow, building by building, as share_by_hour says; the colour is a candle's and a small oil lamp's. Outside: the lighthouse's lantern, and a lantern at the fort's south gate. Liberty L-night-lights-3333 records what is ours.

windows.basis: The town made and sold its own light: the Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833 carries Daniel Elston's soap and candle manufactory, 'paying cash for tallow and house ashes', and Philo Carpenter's drugs, medicines and 'oils' (chicago_democrat_1833_11_26); the Army's ration carried candles, a pound and a half to every hundred rations in the act of 1802, a quarter of an ounce a man a day (us_statutes_1802_military_peace_establishment, sec. 6). Light that cost money was burned in the evening and put out for the night. The hours table itself is ours.

lights.label: The lighthouse's light, in its lantern room
lights.basis: The tower 'employed four, fourteen-inch reflectors in its bird-cage lantern room' and Samuel Lasby was 'keeper of the light, which was the first established on Lake Michigan' (lighthousefriends_chicago; Andreas says 'a fourteen-inch reflector', andreas_1884_v1). A lighthouse is lit from sunset to sunrise; its place is the tower's (chicago_lighthouse_1832 placement, Wright 1834) at the middle of the modelled lantern cage, 9.0 to 11.0 m up. Its brightness, colour and the glow's size are ours.

lights.label: A lantern at the fort's south gate, by the guard house
lights.basis: Hubbard names a guard-house beside the southern gate in 1827 (andreas_1884_v1, read for fort_dearborn_guard_house); a guard kept the gate. That the sentry had a lantern, and that it hung here, is ours.
